why: Scenario: L1 makes a hard stop while the ego follows in the same lane. The ranges are within the simulator's braking, time, and distance limits; h0_decel stays below dry-road mu*g. Exposure 0.05 per trip is an illustrative prior, not a measured incidence rate. Its scale is anchored to the SHRP2 NDS finding that a median driver experienced about one 0.3g braking event per mile on low-speed neighborhood roads; this severe close-following subset should be rarer and needs local fleet naturalistic data to calibrate. Source: Gibran Ali, Characterizing Human Driving Behavior Through an Analysis of Naturalistic Driving Data, Virginia Tech dissertation (2023), https://vtechworks.lib.vt.edu/items/6bb2f65a-7a19-4a6d-a9e1-717ad5f5b5fb.
